summary: A minimalist bluffing and deduction game where each turn you play one of just two cards in hand, using character powers to guess, compare, or eliminate opponents. Rounds are over in minutes, and the tension comes almost entirely from reading what little information is available about who holds what.
praised: extremely fast to teach and play
surprisingly tense bluffing and deduction from a tiny card pool
great icebreaker or filler between heavier games
scales well from two players up to larger groups
criticised: outcomes can feel very swingy and luck-driven, especially in short rounds
player elimination within a round can leave someone waiting
limited strategic depth for players wanting a serious game

interaction.kind: direct targeted card effects (guessing/eliminating/forcing discards) aimed at specific opponents each turn
interaction.detail: Nearly every card played names another player and directly threatens their hand or survival — there is essentially no private engine to build, only your one card and your read on opponents. The entire small game state (who's still in, who holds what) is shared and contested.
interaction.said: reviewers regularly call it "pure take-that" and "you're always targeting someone" — cards exist almost entirely to eliminate or expose opponents

sources: Favor tokens for winning a round
scoring.how_you_win: Win individual rounds by being the last player left or holding the highest card when the deck runs out to earn a favor token; the first to collect the target number of tokens (set by player count) wins the match.
scoring.score_note: target tokens needed drops as player count rises
